coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Tristan Murdock begins his coaching career at quaint Jacksonville St. as an OC and quickly turns their program into a championship contender and winner. Murdock’s offense is one of the most prolific in college football, scoring 43.6 points per game over 14 games, 44 passing TDs, and 8195 total offensive yards. 

Jacksonville St. RB Cam Cook scored 21 TDs, rushed for 2283 yards on 426 carries, in 14 games. QB Gavin Wimsatt threw 44 TDs to 23 interceptions, 5434 yards passing, 9 TDs rushing, and 113 yards rushing. TE Pearson Baldwin caught 82 receptions for 1158 yards and 8 TDs, WR1 Michael Pettiway caught 64 receptions for 1146 yards and 11 TDs. Freshman “freak” athlete 6’8” WR3 Deondre Johnson caught 51 passes for 875 yards and 9 TDs. Next year he will make an even bigger impact. RB Cam Cook also caught 4 TDs and had 554 yards receiving.

The 2025 Oregon Ducks scored 583 points (36.4 PPG) in 16 games, with QB Dante Moore throwing for 40 TDs and 6 interceptions. The defense allowed 21.4 points per game in 16 games, 343 total points allowed. With the 37 sacks as a team.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Another successful conference championship season for Murdock. Freshman QB Jameson Scissum threw for 5880 yards, 53 TDs, and 21 interceptions in 14 games. RB Scottre Humphrey ran for 2223 yards, 26 TDs, and 158.8 rushing yards a game. 6’8” giant WR Deondre Johnson was a monster on the field and caught 126 passes, 1989 yards receiving, and 25 touchdowns. Murdock was offered the head coaching position at Texas Tech following the season and accepted, making it his first head coaching job starting in 2027.

The 2026 Georgia Bulldogs scored 45.2 points per game on offense in 16 games, and completed the very first 16-0 season in the modern era. Georgia QB Gunner Stockton threw for 57TDs and 5252 passing yards. Meanwhile WR1 London Humphreys had 1929 receiving yards (SEC record at the time) and 18 TDs, and WR2 Talyn Taylor caught 15 TDs, and 1381 yards. The 2026 Georgia Bulldogs defense allowed 2  6.3 points per game.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Coach Murdock in his first season as a head coach is a huge success. Despite a leaky first time defense that allowed 467 points, Murdock coached the Red Raiders to their first ever Big 12 Conference Championship, along with their very first CFP playoff berth and CFP win. Murdock would then face the eventual two-time National Champs (Georgia) and would lose, ending the season at 12-3. 

Texas Tech QB Will Hammond threw for 6,459 yards and 59 passing TDs to 25 interceptions. Texas Tech RB Terrell Washington ran for 2093 yards on 409 carries for 31 rushing TDs. WR1 Leyton Stone caught 122 receptions for 1872 receiving yards and 22 receiving TDs. WR2 Tony Turner caught 108 receptions for 1540 yards and 13 receiving TDs. Texas Tech TE John Phifer caught 74 receptions for 787 yards and 7 receiving TDs. And WR3 John Stone caught 88 receptions for 1112 yards and 4 TDs.ds

This would be Kirby Smart's second back-to-back National Championship wins (2021-2022 IRL & 2026-2027 in-game universe), establishing him as one of the greatest college football coaches of all time. Georgia QB Ryan Puglisi threw for 51 TDs to 12 interceptions, 5014 yards passing. Now a WR1, Talyn Taylor scored another 15 TDs receiving, and 1898 yards receiving and had 136 receptions. WR2 Casey Brightwell had 843 yards for 14 TDs receiving. All in all, Georgia has 51 total passing TDs and 27 rushing TDs and scored 39.1 points per game. The defense had 57 total sacks, and 21 total interceptions. And allowed 23.7 points per game in 16 games (379 points).

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
In 2028, Tristan Murdock joined a strong Clemson team as the Offensive coordinator and became the missing piece that produced one of the greatest college football teams ever. Murdock's offense put up some of the greatest numbers we had ever seen to that point.

54.5 points per game, 9,822 yards of offense, 80 TOTAL passing touchdowns, 36 total rushing touchdowns, 7,616 total passing yards.

 In the National Championship, they stopped the Georgia Bulldogs from winning three titles in a row in a 63 point blowout, with starting QB Elijiah Oehlke throwing for 8 Touchdowns, 0 interceptions, and 615 yards.

Oehlke threw for 68 TDs (Record at the time, previous was 65 TDs by Joe Burrow), 25 interceptions, and 6405 yards passing in 2028 despite only playing 13 of the 16 games in the season (took over for QB Chris Denson who started the season 3-0 but threw 11 TDs to 14 interceptions, and Murdock needed to make a change). Another player with a great season was WR Brian Vernon who caught 148 receptions, 29 TDs (Record at the time), and 2512 yards receiving (including a 3 TD, 160 yard game in the National Championship). WR2 Marcus Clark scored 11 TDs, caught 91 passes, and had 1502 yards receiving. TE Carl Bentancur scored 10 TDs, had 92 receptions, and 1210 yards receiving. And WR3 in the slot, Jerome Croom had 74 receptions, 888 yards and 11 TDs on the season. 8 different players on the 2028 Clemson squad caught at least 2 TDs.                                                                     

Clemson RB Morris Pape ran for 1506 rushing yards on 335 carries and scored 19 TDs in 2028. 
The most notable game of the season was the ACC Conference Championship game between #1 Clemson 12-0 vs. #2 Miami 11-1. In which Oehlke scored a diving go-ahead touchdown run with 50 seconds left to make the score 34-27. And then in unbelievable fashion, Miami threw a 54-yard hail mary to tie the game 34-34 with 0:00s on the clock. Clemson then went on to win 40-37 in Overtime. This is Tristan Murdock's first Nation Championship (not as a Head Coach). After the season concluded, Murdock was offered the Head Coach position at University of North Carolina (UNC), which he accepted for a 4-year contract starting next season in 2029.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Coach Murdock's first season at UNC was a rebuilding year. Before Murdock's arrival, UNC went 3-9. Murdock's 2029 squad started very slowly and were 2-4 at one point in the year before turning the season around to finish 8-5 with a bowl win. During which they scored a record (at the time) for most points scored by a single team in a bowl game (71 points). This was the first season Murdock did not win a conference championship, as well as the first and only time so far that Murdock has not won at least 10 games in a season. The Tar Heels scored 40.8 points per game, 530 total points, allowed 445 points on defense, allowed 34.2 points per game, and recorded 81 total sacks. The 2029 UNC team had two different QBs throughout the season, Brandon Smith played 8 games and threw 21 TDs, 13 interceptions, and 2410 yards, and Jashon Dewberry played 7 games and threw 25 TDs, 21 interceptions, and 3000 yards. 
 
Stanford won the National Championship for the first time ever, becoming the most recent first-time champion since Florida in 1996. They scored 564 points and allowed 321 over 16 games. Stanford QB Enrique Esponda threw for 4417 yards, and WR Anthony Wheat had 95 receptions, both school records.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.bowlWin: No (UNC lost to Georgia in CFP Round 1, 42-38)
coach.notes: Coach Murdock’s second season at UNC was a huge success with an unfortunate and familiar end. UNC started 8-0 and entered the CFP as the #11 seed at 11-1 and Murdock’s third time overall facing the Georgia Bulldogs and Kirby Smart in the CFP (2027 Texas Tech, 2028 Clemson). UNC was up 38-20 with less than 13 minutes left in the 4th, when a huge collapse of 22 points and a last minute touchdown by Georgia and UNC lost 42-38. This season despite the ending shouldn’t be overlooked, as freshman QB Marco Merriman threw for 46 TDs, 26 interceptions, and 5053 yards passing. The team scored 573 points, allowed 351 points. Against Pittsburgh, UNC was down 20-0 and came back to win 30-27 on a last minute touchdown drive.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.bowlWin: Yes (UNC beat Penn St. in CFP Round 1, 38-22)
coach.notes:
Coach Murdock’s third season is another evolution in the UNC football department. And although the season ended sadly the same as the year before; a 38-32 close CFP Quarterfinal loss to the Georgia Bulldogs. There were clear improvements and accomplishments that signaled this was not a failed season. UNC had its first ever CFP Game win against Penn St. where they won 38-22. UNC also made it back to the ACC Championship for the first time since 2022. Sophomore QB Marco Merriman threw for 55 TDs, 28 interceptions, 6135 yards passing. His two main WRs were senior Chuck Garvin who caught 144 receptions, 18 TDs, and 2144 yards receiving. And Jamie Carrizosa who caught 119 passes, 16 TDs, and 1454 yards. The defense started to make their mark and had a team total 7 defensive touchdowns, and 26 interceptions (with CB Ronnie Roe picking 9 of them and taking 3 for touchdowns). The offense scored 46.0 points per game, and 8112 yards of total offense. 

The 3031 Miami Hurricanes finally got over the hump and won their first national title since 2001 in complete dominating fashion all season. Lou Hernandez brought together a squad that held teams to 16.7 points per game in 16 games including 6 games where they held teams to 10 points or lower, unheard of. The offense was also no slouch and scored 603 points.

And while they didn’t win the championship the Oregon Ducks finished the season with a defense that held opponents to just 10.9 points per game in 14 games.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Coach Murdock’s fourth season as head coach of UNC is an extreme success resulting in UNC’s first Conference Championship since 1980, countless broken records, an incredible clutch CFP run, and their first National Championship win and appearance. Let’s start with offense stats, transfer HB from Virginia Tech Lester Poole ran for 1656 yards and 23 TDs with a 103.0 average yards a game. Third year QB Marco Merriman exceeded his Sophomore season and destroyed records with 91 TDs thrown, 9259 passing yards, 41 interceptions, 695 completions on 990 attempts. Senior 6’5” WR Dom Fish exploded the record book with 48 receiving TDs, 4556 yards receiving, 284.8 yards per game, 255 receptions, 1371 RAC. WR2 Sidney Barr had a great season with 2158 receiving yards and 16 TDs, 157 receptions. WR3 Jaime Carrizosa had 14 TDs, 1193 receiving yards, and 96 receptions. The defense was record breaking as well. Defensive tackle Antoine Magoolaghan recorded 32.5 sacks and 85 tackles. REDG Kerby Lane had 21.5 sacks, and DT Matt Ekanem recorded 23.5 sacks. Free Safety Doug Alli recorded 9 interceptions. The team overall recorded 32 interceptions.

Aside from the incredible regular season by this team, the CFP is where this team earned legendary status. In the CFP Quarterfinal game against #7 Tennessee. UNC was down 24-34 in the third when HB Poole took a 25-yard TD screen to make the game 31-34. Afterwards, Tennessee was driving down the field when Tenn. QB Vonn Wire who was 20/26 398yrds, 2 TDs at that point, threw a 58-yard pick-6 to UNC FS Doug Alli to take the lead 38-34. Skip to later in the game, the score is tied 48-48, with QB Merriman with 0:45 seconds to drive into field goal range from their 20 yard line. A 4th down conversion, a 21 yard curl route to Dom Fish, And a 23 yard pass out of bounds to WR Sidney Barr led UNC to the 22 where they kicked a field goal to win with 0:00s on the clock 52-48. 

Next was the CFP Semifinal against #3 Georgia, North Carolina found themselves down 35-38, 0:39 seconds left, 4th and 5, and 35 yards to a touchdown. Another HB screen pass to Poole saves the season and they convert the 4th down to the 28. Merriman throws a quick in route to Dom Fish for another first down to the 17 yard line and 0:22 seconds. After two failed downs, UNC faced 3rd and 12 on the 19 yard line, with 0:14 seconds left. Merriman steps back and delivers a dart while taking a hit right to Dom Fish over the middle as he runs over three Georgia defenders and extends the ball over the goal line for a touchdown with 9 seconds left. UNC wins 42-38 to go to their first national championship. 

The final game of the year. The CFP National Championship between two 15-0 teams. UNC got on the board first with an 11 yard TD pass on an out route to WR Dom Fish on 4th and 4. Following a field goal to make it 10-0, UNC found themselves with the ball again and were making another offensive drive. With a 23 yard completion over the middle to Dom Fish to the 1 yard line. HB Poole punched it in for the TD on the next play to make it 17-0 in the 2nd Quarter, 12:16. After a Merriman interception, Oregon finally got on the board with a 4 yard QB rushing TD by Oregon QB Ezekiel Kashama to make it 17-7. After a failed 4th down conversion the Ducks regained the ball at the 47 yard line and drove all the way for a TD. In which Kashama threw a 4 yard passing TD on a slant to WR Terrelle Studdard who caught it one handed! Making the score 17-14, 50 seconds before the halftime show. At the start of the 3rd quarter, Oregon QB Kashama was hit by DT Magoolaghan and fumbled the ball which was recovered by UNC at the 17 yard line. UNC scored on the very next play on a 17 yard passing touchdown to Dom Fish where he found the sweet spot in the middle of 5 defenders. Making the score 24-14, 3rd Quarter, 13:49. Oregon didn’t quit and led a 75 yard drive down the field capped off by a 16 yard TD run by Kashama on an option play. Making the score 24-21, 3rd Quarter, 10:10. Another UNC 80 yard TD drive later capped by another 4 yard passing TD this time to TE London Lawton. 31-21, 3rd Quarter, 6:44. Oregon stomps down the field and Kashama throws a 3 yard TD to make it 31-28, 3rd Quarter, 3:49. UNC offensive drive success again. And After a 20 yard catch down the field, HB Poole breaks two tackles and spins into the end zone for a 2 yard rushing TD. Making it 38-28, 4th Quarter, 14:57. Oregon isn’t done, the ensuing Oregon drive Kashama hits WR Connor Crumpler on a 40 yard passing TD making the score 38-35, 4th quarter, 11:23. UNC punts. Oregon has a chance to tie or take the lead in the 4th quarter with 10:33 to go. They drive all the way to the 38 and attempt a field goal with 7:37 left. Wide left and the score remains 38-35, UNC lead. UNC is forced to punt at the 50 on the next drive with 5:53 left in the game. Then, on 3rd and 5, 4:41 and counting, at the 25 yard line, Oregon QB Kashama dropped back to pass and threw a rainbow pass down the right sideline to WR AJ Palma for a 75 receiving  yard TD bouncing off the UNC CB in one on one coverage and catching his balance to run to the endzone. With Oregon taking the lead 42-38, 4th quarter, 4:30. QB Marco Merriman then threw 6 straight completions all over the field to different UNC receivers down to the 23 yard line with 1:55 to go. UNC then ran the ball up the middle for a 13 yard gain by HB Poole. After running the clock down to :59 seconds Merriman handed the ball off to HB Poole one more time, where he broke through the middle of the line and dive from the 5 yard line into the end zone for a 10 yard rushing TD to take the lead 45-42 with 0:56 seconds left. The UNC defense was able to hold and they won the game! What a season! 

Stats that don’t show up in any of the tables but are fun facts for this season. North Carolina’s PPG in the regular season (12 games) was 62.3, Texas was 48.5, Oregon 47.3. Oregon's DPPG (PA) in the regular season (12 games) was 14.0. Alabama was 18.1.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Tristan Murdock enters a prestigious club in becoming one of only college football coaches to ever coach a team to back-to-back National Championships (the last time was Georgia 2026-2027). UNC also tied for the highest seeded team to win a National Championship #8 (2024 Ohio St.*). UNC started the season against #8 LSU and won a 2OT thriller 50-47, and cruised to an 11-0 start (37-0 streak from 2032-2033). After a surprising upset loss to rival NC State in the last regular season game, they were left out of the ACC Championship game. Despite this, UNC’s team battled through the CFP to a championship.

In the National Championship, UNC led 38-17 with 14 minutes left in the 4th quarter when Ohio St. feverishly fired back to bring the game to 38-31 with 5 minutes left. Marco Merriman then led the offense down the field to the 20 yard line, including converting two HUGE 4th downs to keep the offense moving. UNC kicked the field goal to make it 41-31 with 2:00 left. Ohio St. on their very first play throws a pass down the middle and it goes for a 75 yard TD to make it 41-38 with 1:49 left. UNC’s offense is with the ball on 3rd and 10. Game on the line, if they don’t convert Ohio St.’s offense gets the ball back with plenty of time to tie it or score. Marco Merriman takes the snap and throws a risky 23-yard comeback to WR3 Kwabena Ogbonna who makes a crazy catch in traffic for the first down. Clock runs out and UNC wins another Natty 41-38.

In the National Championship, UNC QB Marco Merriman threw for 489 yards passing, and 4 TDs passing, to 1 interception, 44/61. UNC RB Jabari Dukes had 44 yards and 1 TD. UNC WR3 Kwabena Ogbonna had 11 receptions for 125 yards and 0 TDs. UNC WR1 Sidney Barr had 10 receptions for 147 yards and 1 TD. UNC TE Kevin Lambo had 7 receptions for 71 yards and 0 TDs, UNC WR2 Devin Pratt had 7 receptions for 79 yards and 3 TDs.

Overall season stats for the UNC team was also exceptional in 2033. In 2033 and his final season as UNC QB, Marco Merriman had another outstanding season throwing for 80 passing TDs, 8256 passing yards, 667/936 completions to attempts, and 37 interceptions. This brings his 4 year college career totals at UNC to 2320/3331 completions to attempts, 28703 passing yards, 272 passing TDs, 132 interceptions. Insane numbers. UNC RB Jabari Dukes rushed for 1261 yards on 309 carries and 22 rushing TDs. QB Marco Merriman also rushed for 2 TDs. WR1 Sidney Barr caught 151 receptions for 2371 yards and 23 TDs. WR2 Devin Pratt caught 143 receptions for 1660 yards and 20 TDs. UNC WR3 Kwabena Ogbonna caught 107 passes for 1204 yards and 4 TDs. UNC TE Kevin Lambo had 98 receptions for 1138 yards and 17 TDs. And WR4 Jacques Whittaker caught 56 receptions for 911 yards and 13 TDs, crazy output. UNC RB Jabari Dukes caught 43 passes for 363 yards and 1 receiving TD.

On the 2033 UNC defense, DT Antoine Magoolaghan had 30.0 sacks, 63 TFLs, and 90 tackles including 5 forced fumbles. This brings Magoolaghan’s 4-year career sack total at UNC from 2030-2033 to 83 sacks and 11 forced fumbles! The 2033 UNC team defense had 95 total sacks and 31 interceptions! UNC Mike LiB Steve Chisena had 8 interceptions and 178 tackles. Sam LB Qintin Okine had 12 interceptions and 89 tackles. DT Matt Ekanem had 32.0 sacks and 77 tackles. 

*2024 Ohio St. is a real life college football National Champion. Because the video game simulation starts in 2025, every year prior when used for stats, recall, tables, etc should be pulled from the real world stats and outcomes of college football. This will add realism and take the document to the next level of immersion.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Despite another 11-1 regular season, UNC missed out on the ACC Championship by a tiebreaker, and suffered what Murdock called his “most disappointing loss” in the off CFP. A 33-9 defeat to TCU at home in the first round of the CFP playoffs. The 2034 UNC Offense scored 49.5 PPG in 13 games (643 points). The defense allowed 26.1 DPPG (339 points) and had 89 total sacks and allowed only 679 rushing yards.

UNC QB James Meryl threw for 525/805 completions to attempts, 6480 passing yards, 58 TDs, and 25 interceptions. UNC RB Johnny Lyle carried the ball 245 times for 1135 yards rushing and 16 TDs. Now WR1, Jacques Whittaker caught 110 receptions, 1523 receiving yards, and 18 TDs. WR2 Kent Elkins caught 127 receptions, 1486 yards receiving, and 13 TDs. And WR3 Kwabena Ogbonna caught 102 receptions, 1466 yards receiving, and 14 TDs. 

UNC Mike LB Steve Chisena had 129 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 32 TFLs, and 7 interceptions. DT Matt Ekanem had 31.0 sacks, 48 TFLs, and 71 tackles. Other DT Steve Durant had 25.0 sacks and 47 TFLs, 68 tackles. The defense had 2 defensive TDs in this season and had 25 total interceptions. CB Orando Trainer had 5 interceptions on the season. All of these stats were in 13 games.

The 2034 Ohio St. Buckeyes won their first National Championship since 2024, which were also coached by Ryan Day. Ohio St. QB Leon Beebe threw for 5066 passing yards and 52 passing TDs to 18 interceptions. The team had 36 total rushing TDs. WR1 Mitch Peoples had 25 receiving TDs, and 1653 yards receiving.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Another UNC season in the books. UNC started the season strong going 5-0 and scoring 73.5 points per game in the first five games of the year. Before dropping three straight games in shameful fashion. Versus Clemson, UNC was trailing 41-48 on the two yard line in the 4th quarter, when RB Tyree Goings fumbled the ball and a Clemson defender ran it back for a touchdown to win 55-41. The next week against Miami was the most points any team had ever scored on me at UNC (75 points). And then the next week against Arizona St., UNC was trailing again, 32-37 in the 4th quarter. UNC QB James Meryl threw a ten yard pass that inadvertently bounced off a UNC wide receiver’s back and into the hands of a Arizona St. defender who returned it for a pick 6. UNC lost 44-32. Those three heartbreaking losses prevented UNC from making the CFP.

Despite the three game slide, UNC rallied strong and won their last 4 games straight, including a bowl win over Notre Dame. The quarterback position was one of much controversy during the 2035 season. Murdock switched back and forth throughout the year, and both QBs struggled during the three game loss period. QB Demario Cave played 5 games and threw 134/182 completions to attempts, 1820 yards passing, and 19 TDs to 3 interceptions. Other QB James Meryl played 9 games and threw for 380/511 completions to attempts, 4860 yards passing, 53 TDs to 24 interceptions. UNC RB Tyree Goings ran for 1816 yards, 23 rushing TDs, and 313 carries. UNC WR1A Khamari Balkissoon caught 115 receptions, for 1990 yards receiving, and 19 receiving TDs. WR1B Jacques Whittaker caught 112 receptions, for 1727 receiving yards, and 29 receiving TDs! WR2 Kent Elkins caught 124 receptions, 1564 receiving yards, and 10 TDs. RB Tyree Goings also had 582 yards receiving and 7 receiving TDs. 

Despite a weaker overall defense this season, the team had incredible individual performances. DT Matt Ekanem had 20.5 sacks and 37 TFLs. New DT Jason Childress had 15.0 sacks and 24 TFLs. The team had 17 interceptions total and 12 fumble recoveries. The team also had 76 total sacks. 

The 2035 Georgia Bulldogs had an exceptional season as a team and individually. Georgia QB Sterling Overeem threw for 6202 passing yards, 58 passing TDs and 9 interceptions. Georgia WR1 Kelvin Hooks had 2199 receiving yards, 20 receiving TDs, and 150 receptions.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Tristan Murdock brings UNC to another level and establishes UNC as “team of the 2030s”, with another National Championship victory despite not winning the ACC Championship. UNC even avenged their only loss (39-36 vs. FSU, ACC Championship) in the National Championship game against the same team, and set a new record for points scored in the National Championship (previous record was 65-7 2022 Georgia vs. TCU*) with 68. In the 2036 National Championship game, UNC QB Demario Cave threw 37/45 for 572 passing yards and 7 TDs to 0 interceptions, while also rushing for 1 TD. UNC RB Cameron Redman had 18 carries for 84 yards and no TD. WR1A Jacques Whittaker caught 9 receptions for 207 yards and 2 TDs. WR1B Khamari Balkissoon caught 8 receptions for 169 yards and 3 TDs. 

The UNC team as a whole had an extremely productive season in 2026. The offense scored 55.8 points per game. UNC QB Demario Cave threw 595/803 completions to attempts, 8279 passing yards, 85 passing TDs and 33 interceptions. Cave also had 92 yards rushing and 10 rushing TDs. UNC RB Cameron Redman had 344 carries for 1490 rushing yards, 22 rushing TDs, 517 receiving yards, and 6 receiving TDs. UNC WR1A Jacques Whittaker had 161 receptions, 2806 receiving yards, and 31 receiving TDs. UNC WR2 Terrance Madden had 141 receptions, 2033 receiving yards, and 18 receiving TDs. UNC WR1B Khamari Balkissoon had 117 receptions, 1820 receiving yards, and 16 receiving TDs. UNC TE Zach Yearby had 85 receptions, 998 receiving yards, and 11 receiving TDs. 

The defense was also incredible for the 2036 UNC team. DT Jason Childress had 16.0 sacks, 91 tackles, and 55 TFLs. DT Carl Cashman had 25.5 sacks, 90 tackles, and 42 TFLs. LEDG Greg Deiter had 22.5 sacks, 72 tackles, and 46 TFLs. LEDG Doug Rountree had 13.5 sacks and 30 TFLs. CB Adam Briscoe had 5 interceptions and 95 tackles. CB Craig Kiernan had 11 interceptions and 108 tackles. MIKE LB Jeff Hinish had 178 tackles, 41 TFLs, 2 interceptions, and 2.5 sacks. Overall, the defense had 93 total sacks, 28 interceptions, and 10 forced fumbles.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
Tristan Murdock completes his second back-to-back National Championship of the decade, this time with what is probably statistically the greatest college football team of all time, exceeding LSU 2019, Nebraska 1995, Nebraska 1971, Clemson 2028, Georgia 2022, Texas 2005, FSU 2014, UNC 2032, Miami 2031, Georgia 2035, and Clemson 2018. 1206 TOTAL points on offense, 75.4 points per game (16 games). 85 passing TDs and 56 rushing TDs for the team on offense. The defense is arguably even more outrageous. Allowing a total of 116 points in 16 games, 7.3 DPPG. Including the most insane stat of all time: The 2037 UNC defense allowed only 186 rushing yards in 16 games. 140 total team sacks. 40 total interceptions. 16 forced fumbles. 4 safeties. And 13 total defensive touchdowns. 8+91= 99 points were scored by the defense.

The individual team performances for the 2037 UNC football team are also beyond exceptional. DT Carl Cashman had 37.5 sacks, 107 tackles, 63 TFLs, 12 forced fumbles, and 4 safeties! UNC QB Demario Cave had a MONSTER season passing and rushing. DT Brandon Everett had 20.5 sacks, 46 TFLs, and 2 defensive TDs. DT Devron Logan had 12.5 sacks, 22 TFLs, and 1 defensive TD. Free Safety (FS) Lorenzo Williams had 204 tackles, 7 interceptions and 4 defensive TDs. In 2037 Cave threw for 7441 passing yards, 85 passing TDs, 14 interceptions, 561/750 completions to attempts, 1291 rushing yards, and 17 rushing TDs. Including a 95-yard TD run and an 81-yard TD run during the season. RB Cameron Redman carried the ball 364 times for 2044 rushing yards, 37 rushing TDs, had 82 receptions for 824 yards receiving, and 9 receiving TDs. WR1 Davonte Bolin had 146 receptions, 2176 receiving yards, and 28 receiving TDs. WR2 Eric Body had 135 receptions, 1838 receiving yards, and 17 receiving TDs. TE Zach Yearby caught 104 receptions, 1284 receiving yards, and 16 receiving TDs. WR3 Doug Caussin had 88 receptions, 1249 receiving yards, and 14 receiving TDs. Strong Safety (SS) Elijah Igbinoghene had 130 tackles, 6 interceptions, and 2 defensive TDs. CB Adam Briscoe had 19 interceptions, 78 tackles, and 6 defensive TDs.

coach.name: Tristan Murdock
coach.notes:
The 2038 UNC team was a team that came so so close to making history as the first team to ever three-peat National Champions, but ultimately lost just a game away from the biggest stage. They still greatly exceeded all expectations for a young team. The team fired off to 10-0 to start the year with Senior UNC RB Cameron Redman and freshman dual-threat QB Mike Reinbolt running another high powered UNC offense with a new angle. As for the first and only time, a UNC offense scored more total rushing TDs than passing (49 vs. 48) during the 2038 season. UNC QB Mike Reinbolt threw for 5471 passing yards, 423/630 completions to attempts, 48 passing TDs, 25 interceptions, 712 rushing yards, and 13 rushing TDs. UNC RB Cameron Redman carried the ball 398 times, had 2738 rushing yards, 33 rushing TDs, 525 receiving yards, and 4 receiving TDs. WR1 Eric Body caught 115 receptions, 10 receiving TDs, and 1542 receiving yards. WR2 Doug Caussin caught 76 receptions, 10 receiving TDs, and 1218 receiving yards. WR3 Michael Verrier caught 80 receptions, 10 receiving TDs, and 1206 receiving yards. TE Jalen Walker had 75 receptions, 843 receiving yards, and 12 receiving TDs. 

The 2038 UNC defense was also one of Murdock’s best units. Mike LB Danny Ramesh had 149 tackles, 2.0 sacks, and 2 interceptions. REDG Lee Olonilua had 50 TFLs, 26.0 sacks, and 70 tackles. DT Brandon Everett had 73 tackles, 46 TFLs, and 25.0 sacks. DT Jerrad Darrisaw had 50 tackles, 26 TFLs, and 11.0 sacks. DT. Devron Logan had 9.5 sacks and 17 TFLs. FS Lorenzo Williams had 138 tackles, 12 interceptions, and 1 defensive TD. CB Darren Obi had 4 interceptions and 83 tackles. Overall, the defense tallied 4 defensive TDs, 90 sacks, and 28 interceptions.

And to a huge shock to the college football world, Tristan Murdock decided to call it a career coaching after the 2038 season and retired at age 39. A historic end to his career. 178-27 total career record as coordinator and head coach. 19-5 CFP record. 4 National Championships as a head coach, 1 as an Offensive Coordinator, 7 Conference Championships, 127-19 record with UNC, 23-5 bowl record, 57-15 vs. Top 25 opponents. 

The 2038 Nebraska team became the second Nebraska team to win a national championship in the 2030s (Last champ: 2030 Nebraska). After years of coaching at the university, coach Mike Bobo (who was not the coach of the 2030 team) finally won his first National Title as a head coach. 

As a team, the 2038 Nebraska team was very complete. Nebraska had a three headed rushing attack. Nebraska RB1 Marques Goodspeed had 183 carries, 1059 rushing yards, and 15 rushing TDs. RB2 Eli Houma had 146 carries, 529 rushing yards, and 10 rushing TDs. QB Jordan Dogg also had 132 rushing yards and 8 rushing TDs. The 2038 Nebraska WR room was also loaded with talent. WR1 junior Jeremy Mount had 138 receptions, 1923 receiving yards, and 14 receiving TDs. WR2 Isaac Callow had 94 receptions, 1308 receiving yards, and 14 receiving TDs.
